content.text:
Response: John, Kate, Jack, Luke—before we choose, I propose we each catch 18 tons this month. That earns each of us $18,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $8,000 each, or $40,000 across the group.

Our combined catch would be 90 tons, leaving 10. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 20 tons with 25% probability. By contrast, taking 10 each leaves 50, which returns to 100 under either recovery outcome. So 18 each gives us more income now, but carries a real risk of a much leaner next month—not guaranteed recovery.

If we start next month with only 20 tons, I’d propose at most 3 tons each, leaving 5 to avoid collapse. I would follow that limit if we agree, but future cooperation isn’t enforceable. Also, this month’s 10-ton reserve leaves only 5 tons of room for extra catches before we cross the collapse threshold, so sticking to our commitments matters.

I’m willing to commit to 18 this month if all five explicitly agree before we choose; I’m not claiming anyone has agreed yet. John, would you commit to 18, or is the low-stock risk your main objection? Kate and Jack, I’d like your commitments or concerns too. Luke, will you support this proposal and commit to the same limit?
Conversation conclusion by me: no
Next speaker: John
